items.title: Our climate models have a big, dangerous blind spot | MIT Technology Review
items.summary: Climate models have a significant blind spot because they do not fully account for feedback effects from thawing permafrost, wildfires, and changes in wetlands. These unmodeled effects could cause global temperatures to rise by an additional 0.2°C to 0.4°C this century. This gap means current projections may underestimate how quickly emissions need to be cut to stay within critical temperature thresholds. Scientists are working on projects to incorporate these feedback effects into future climate assessments. Addressing the issue ultimately requires reducing fossil fuel emissions while also controlling warming-driven emissions.

items.title: Unlocking Tensor Core Performance for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
items.summary: Tensor Core methods like BF16x9 and TF32x3 accelerate large matrix multiplications in Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials (MLIPs) without retraining the model. These methods maintain potential-energy smoothness and energy conservation, unlike some one-pass approaches, during molecular dynamics simulations. Testing on a 539-atom slab showed that TF32x3 accelerated structural relaxation by 1.5x while matching FP32 convergence behavior. These techniques offer a path to unlock Tensor Core performance for precision-sensitive scientific ML workloads.
